slides.title: This trinomial has ==two== answers. Most give one.

slides.stem: If 4x² + kx + 49 is a perfect-square trinomial, what are the possible values of k?
slides.prompt: Time yourself. Comment your time and your answer.

slides.title: C — 28 or −28
slides.body: (2x ± 7)² = 4x² ± 28x + 49, so k = 28 or k = −28. Most students pick A (28 only): considers only a = 7 and misses the negative case.

slides.title: Find k for Perfect Square Trinomial (Both Signs)
slides.body: A perfect-square trinomial a² ± 2ab + b² allows a positive or negative middle term. Unless the problem restricts the sign, both values of k are valid.
